annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "tap" on page 565 ("The Bedroom Scene"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream. During this Age of Men (closing) phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.

annotations.annotation_text: Fraternal archetype "jerry" on page 565 ("The Bedroom Scene"): the opposing sons — Shem the Penman (introvert artist, tree, darkness) and Shaun the Post (extrovert politician, stone, light) — manifest here within HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream. Their Brunonian dialectic of coinciding opposites propels the chapter's conflict during this Age of Men (closing) phase.
sources: Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
